$comment: Intentional, reviewed divergences between an upstream's full rule set and what this package derives. Kept OUT of the generators so a divergence is a declared decision with a reason, never a silent gap. Every generator asserts that a source it parsed to zero rows is listed here; an unlisted zero fails the run.

static_patterns_harmful_content.py.reason: Patterns are built by Python expression evaluation, not static literals: DANGEROUS_ACTIONS concatenates '|'.join(HARMFUL_SUBSTANCES) into each regex at import time, and SUBSTANCE_PATTERNS is an f-string list comprehension over that same list. Deriving them would mean evaluating Python, and a hand-expanded copy would silently rot the moment upstream edits the substance list. This analyzer also targets physical-harm content rather than a software-supply-chain or agent-security property, so it is outside this package's scope.

hooks-background-process.reason: AgentShield v1.4.0 declares this id twice in src/rules/hooks.ts (lines 1021 and 1955) with different names and check bodies — 'Hook Spawns Background Process' and 'Hook Runs Background Process'. Both are real detectors, so neither is dropped; the second occurrence is emitted as `agentshield:hooks-background-process-2`. Revisit when upstream deduplicates.
